pr_comments: Thanks, @MikeMcQuaid. Why did you add `.3` to `HOMEBREW_REQUIRED_RUBY_VERSION`?
@maxim-belkin That's the required system version on macOS (that we're checking in `brew doctor`) and it's easier to discard the parts we don't need for supported versions.
Let's see how this goes, thanks for your work on this @maxim-belkin!

# Please note we will close your issue without comment if you delete, do not read or do not fill out the issue checklist below and provide ALL the requested information. If you repeatedly fail to use the issue template, we will block you from ever submitting issues to Homebrew again. - [x] ran `brew update` and can still reproduce the problem? - [x] ran `brew doctor`, fixed all issues and can still reproduce the problem? - [x] ran `brew config` and `brew doctor` and included their output with your issue? ## What you were trying to do (and why) Use brewski alias to keep brew and installed formulas up-to-date ``` brewski='brew update && brew upgrade && brew cleanup; brew doctor' ``` See https://superuser.com/a/975878 ## What happened (include command output) Next `brew` command (e.g. `brew doctor` run as last in `brewski` alias or `brew config`) that gets to be run after running `brew cleanup`, includes an ugly error message:
Command output

comments:
@sslavic Can you paste the `brew cleanup` removal messaging too? I'm looking for e.g. `brew cleanup; brew config; brew cleanup; brew config` output? Thanks!

CC @maxim-belkin that the "Error" here probably shouldn't be output given it's able to download and use a portable ruby afterwards?

@MikeMcQuaid thanks for looking into this! There's nothing in `brew cleanup` output, it just completes/exits successfully. 

If before running `brew cleanup` I run any other brew command, it would fetch portable ruby, which would be listed in
```
~ ls -lart /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Homebrew/Library/Homebrew/vendor/portable-ruby/       
total 12
drwxr-xr-x 8 foo foo 4096 Apr 17  2019 2.6.3_1
drwxr-xr-x 4 foo foo 4096 Jun 11 10:34 ..
lrwxrwxrwx 1 foo foo    7 Jun 17 10:55 current -> 2.6.3_1
drwxr-xr-x 3 foo foo 4096 Jun 17 10:55 .
```

After running `brew cleanup` there's only left over broken symlink
```
~ ls -lart /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Homebrew/Library/Homebrew/vendor/portable-ruby/
total 8
drwxr-xr-x 4 foo foo 4096 Jun 11 10:34 ..
lrwxrwxrwx 1 foo foo    7 Jun 17 10:55 current -> 2.6.3_1
drwxr-xr-x 2 foo foo 4096 Jun 17 10:56 .
```

Hope this helps.

@sslavic, could you please install portable ruby and then run `brew cleanup --dry-run`?
@MikeMcQuaid, I think the function at fault is `cleanup_portable_ruby` in `$(brew --repo)/Library/Homebrew/cleanup.rb`.

> @MikeMcQuaid, I think the function at fault is `cleanup_portable_ruby` in `$(brew --repo)/Library/Homebrew/cleanup.rb`.

Yep, for sure. Could you try to adjust that so it uses the same logic as your `ruby.sh` changes? I almost wonder if a pure-bash, undocumented Homebrew command for something like `brew use-portable-ruby` which we can shell out to would be the right call here?

> I almost wonder if a pure-bash, undocumented Homebrew command for something like `brew use-portable-ruby` which we can shell out to would be the right call here?

It might be a good idea (this would allow us to avoid code repetition in two different places in two different languages (Bash/Ruby))  _if_ the cleanup logic has to be similar to that in `ruby.sh`. My feeling is that it shouldn't be really checking if Ruby is usable but that the link is broken or that  a more recent version of portable Ruby is already installed... After all, this is a "cleanup" step, not "verify Homebrew works" step.

> My feeling is that it shouldn't be really checking if Ruby is usable but that the link is broken or that a more recent version of portable Ruby is already installed... After all, this is a "cleanup" step, not "verify Homebrew works" step.

What we're doing primarily here is removing portable Ruby if it's no longer needed i.e. there's a system version that fulfils the same requirement.

> could you please install portable ruby and then run brew cleanup --dry-run?

```
~ brew cleanup --dry-run
Would remove: /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Homebrew/Library/Homebrew/vendor/portable-ruby/2.6.3_1 (4,174 files, 31.4MB)
```

> removing portable Ruby if it's no longer needed i.e. there's a system version that fulfills the same requirement

there is no other Ruby that I'm aware of on my machine - so `brew cleanup` shouldn't remove one previous runs of brew commands resolved?

@sslavic Would you mind running `brew cleanup; brew config; brew cleanup; brew config` and pasting the output here? We've just updated portable Ruby so I want to confirm it's not that that we're seeing here.
